What's new in 1.13.229.0

Improved

  • Lower background memory use, especially on 16 GB Macs. Dooze now uses noticeably less memory while you're away, so it stays fast and stable through long sessions and recorded meetings.
  • More dependable background processing. Your memory items are handled more reliably, even while you're actively using chat.
  • Behind-the-scenes reliability and diagnostics improvements.

What's new in 1.13.222.0

Added

  • Point your Claude agent at a meeting while it's still happening. In the chat panel, type @ and pick the meeting that's recording (it now shows a coral "recording now" tag and reads "Live meeting" so you can't confuse it with a finished one). That links the live meeting to the chat: a coral "Live meeting" pill appears in the composer, and everything said in the meeting rides along with each message you send, so you can ask the agent to build or edit a doc from the conversation as it unfolds and keep steering it with follow-ups. Remove the pill to disconnect. BYO-only (uses your own Claude), so the live transcript stays on your machine.

Changed

  • The agent stops fighting its own sandbox, so it wastes fewer turns and gets to the deliverable faster. It now knows up front that it can't run a local web server (so it writes a self-contained file you open directly instead of trying to start one and failing), and how to make a PDF without the tools the sandbox blocks (it hands back the HTML and tells you to Print to PDF). Developer tools you installed (bun, Homebrew, cargo, and friends) now resolve for the agent's commands, so skills that depend on them just work. And an HTML page the agent builds now opens in your browser in one click from its file chip, instead of only revealing in Finder.

What's new in 1.13.211.0

Added

  • The chat now opens with helpful suggestions instead of a blank box. When you open a fresh chat, Dooze shows a couple of things worth doing right now (ask about what you're looking at, ask about a recent meeting, mark up your screen, record a meeting) plus a short "Build with Dooze" list (a website, a deck, a doc, and more). The suggestions adapt to you: they reflect what you've used, what app you're in, and your meetings, and they rotate so they stay fresh.
  • "Ask about the doc you're working on." When a supported app or website is in front of you (a Google Doc, Slides, Sheets, Figma, Notion, Gmail, and more), the suggestion names it, and clicking it captures your screen and answers about exactly what you're looking at. On a browser it reads the active tab through the extension (URL only, no page contents).
  • Guided "Build with Dooze" intakes. Clicking a build suggestion (deck, doc, spreadsheet, website, app, and more) opens with a short, clear brief of what to give Dooze to get started, including which output format you want (HTML, PowerPoint, Google Slides, Word, Markdown, PDF, Excel, CSV, and so on).

The whole surface can be turned off with defaults write app.dooze.client chatEmptyStateEnabled -bool false.

What's new in 1.13.194.0

New

  • Live meeting notes. Jot quick thoughts during a call and hit Return to save them, stamped to that moment. After the call the Notes tab becomes one editable page — a short summary on top, then your notes. Didn't take any? Dooze fills the page with on-device notes for free. An Enhance button adds decisions, action items and follow-ups without touching your words.
  • Bring your own OpenAI Codex agent (early opt-in). Run your own codex as a coding agent inside Dooze, alongside the Claude one — on your own ChatGPT subscription, sandboxed to the chat's folder with an approval card for every command. Dooze can now install Codex for you (one-tap, signed build), it can ask you clarifying questions, search and read your meetings, and pick GPT-5.6 Sol / Terra / Luna. A sandbox self-test and a runaway time limit keep each turn fenced in.
  • Your own Claude skills and settings work inside the BYO agent. When you chat with your own Claude, it loads your personal setup — custom skills and slash commands come along instead of starting blank. Your meetings, transcripts and memory still never leave your Mac, and Dooze's approval card and sandbox still apply.

Changed

  • "Functions" are now "Skills", with a cleaner / menu and editor. Slash commands (Polish, Summarize, your own saved prompts) are Skills everywhere now. The / menu is redesigned to match the app — grouped by source, each row showing its name over its /command, with an "Add new skill" row and a new Description field. Existing custom skills carry over unchanged.
  • Cleaner agent question cards and a neutral Screenshot button. Multiple-choice questions from an agent use a clean list with inline "Other", and the per-message Screenshot toggle is now a plain neutral button instead of a coral one that read like a warning.
  • Markup & Capture describes itself more precisely. The text shipped with a marked-up screenshot now includes the image size, and arrows and pen strokes carry a label for what they point at, so an agent places every coordinate without needing vision.
  • The meeting recorder's next-meeting card is lighter. A clean outlined box instead of a filled tan block, with the whole "Add or edit calendars" area clickable.

Fixed

  • Voice dictation is more reliable. Dictating into the Ask AI chat now works every time (not just the first), no longer re-attaches context you already cleared, and no longer restarts music you had paused.
  • "Open in Chat" on a meeting starts a fresh conversation instead of dropping the transcript into whatever unrelated chat was already open.
  • Calendar and screen-recording prompts appear correctly. "Connect your calendar" now opens the real permission prompt, first-run screen access shows the macOS dialog, and Record no longer re-pops the screen-recording dialog every time.
  • No more launch freezes. Permission checks and memory-index rebuilds that ran on the main thread at start-up — and a main-thread hang while connecting the Claude/Codex agent — are moved off the launch path, so the window stays responsive.
  • Arrow keys + Enter pick the right skill in the / menu. The highlighted row and the selected item now share one list, so the row you see is the one that runs.

What's new in 1.13.175.0

Added

  • Meetings recorded without headphones now clean up their own echo. When you record a call on your Mac's built-in speakers, the other person's voice bleeds into your microphone, so the transcript used to double their words, label them as "You," and sometimes invent whole sentences during the stretches where you were just listening. After a meeting like that, Dooze now runs a quiet background pass that removes the echo and re-transcribes your side from the cleaned audio, so the transcript reads correctly. It only commits the result when it actually improved things (your original recording is kept untouched otherwise), the notes and memory are built from the clean version, and playback switches to the cleaned audio too. A small "Cleaning up audio…" note shows while it works, with a "Clean up audio" button to re-run it. Everything happens on your Mac.
  • Files your coding agent makes now show up as chips you can open. When you use your own Claude subscription as a coding agent and it writes a file (a report, an HTML page, a spreadsheet), that file now appears right in the chat as a clickable chip instead of a raw path you have to hunt down in Finder. Click the chip to open it in your default app, or use the small button next to it to reveal it in Finder. The chips stick around, so you can scroll back to an older message and reopen whatever the agent made. For safety, files that could run code show a "Show in Finder" action instead of opening directly, build and dependency clutter is filtered out, and everything stays inside that chat's own folder on your Mac.

Fixed

  • Meeting recording no longer crashes when a recording stops or fails to start. A timing bug could crash Dooze while it was closing out a recording's audio or video file, most often the moment you pressed Stop or right when a recording couldn't start (for example when the disk was nearly full). Both the microphone-audio and screen-recording paths are fixed, so recordings finish cleanly instead of taking the app down. Paused stretches of a recording are still saved as silence so the audio stays lined up with the video, and that silence is now tracked accurately even if a recording ends mid-pause.
  • The chat panel no longer jumps to full height on your first message. When you sent the first message in a fresh chat, the panel briefly ballooned to nearly the full screen (pushing the "dooze" header off the top, with a big empty gap under "Thinking…"), then snapped back down to fit once the reply arrived. The panel now grows from the composer up to the reply's real height, with no overshoot.

Fixed

  • Dooze no longer freezes for a few seconds when it starts up. Two things at launch were running on the main thread and could stall the whole app (the spinning beachball) for 5 seconds or more: checking whether Dooze opens at login, and rebuilding the search index for your memory. The login check now runs in the background, and the memory index only rebuilds when it's actually missing or out of date — off the main thread when it does. Launch is snappy again, even with a large memory vault.
  • Connecting your Claude subscription now works even if you don't already have Claude installed. Some people saw "Couldn't verify the download" with no way past it. Dooze downloaded its Claude helper but checked it before making it runnable, so the check always failed for anyone who didn't already have Claude on their Mac. Now the download completes and connects.
  • Clearer, correct setup messages. Running low on disk space now says "Not enough disk space" (it could previously show "No internet connection" by mistake), and Dooze checks there is room before starting the ~220 MB download instead of failing partway through.
  • Flaky connections recover on their own. A dropped connection during the download retries a few times instead of failing on the first hiccup, and cancelling now actually stops the download instead of letting it finish in the background.

Changed

  • The welcome message in chat after setup is refreshed. It now walks through the core loop — record your meetings, mark up your screen, and hand all of it to your agents as context (including bringing an agent into a meeting to work with you live) — plus the two hotkeys for dictating into any app or talking to Dooze, and a link to grab 20 minutes with the team.

Fixed

  • Dooze no longer freezes while it checks your saved sign-in. Reading your session from the macOS Keychain used to happen on the main thread, so a briefly busy or locked Keychain could freeze the whole app for several seconds (the spinning beachball). That work now runs off the main thread, so it can't stall what you're doing.
  • Signing out now always takes, and you won't be quietly signed back in. When several things happened at once (right after launch, or just after you signed out), a background refresh could rarely undo your sign-out. Those races are closed: an explicit sign-out always wins.
  • No more flash of the sign-in screen when you open Dooze already signed in. A returning user goes straight to the app, and a brand-new user starts at sign-in instead of the wrong step.
  • Connecting your Claude subscription during onboarding no longer looks broken. Tapping "Connect" used to flicker and do nothing while Dooze quietly downloaded its Claude helper in the background. Now the row shows the download progressing ("Downloading Claude… 40%"), then a clear "Sign in" step, then "Connected" — both in onboarding and in the setup panel, and the download runs in the background so you can keep going.
  • Sign-in is recoverable when the browser tab gets lost. If the Claude sign-in tab ends up buried behind your other windows, tapping "Sign in" again opens a fresh one instead of leaving you stuck.
  • Setup failures now tell you what went wrong ("No internet connection", "Not enough disk space", "Couldn't start Claude") with a "Try again" button, instead of silently doing nothing.

What's new in 1.13.166.0

Added

  • Your coding agent can now find and read your meetings when you ask it to. If you use your own Claude subscription as a coding agent and say something like "look at my meeting with Eric," it can now search your recorded meetings by name, company, or topic. It matches titles, the people who were there, and what was actually said, so it finds the right meeting even when the name only comes up in the conversation itself, not the title. To read a meeting's full transcript it asks your permission first, with a simple "just this once / always / no" choice. You stay in control: a new setting under Privacy, Claude agent, lets you allow it every time, ask each time (the default), or never let the agent touch your meetings at all. Your meetings stay encrypted on your Mac, and nothing is shared until you say yes.

What's new in dooze 1.13.127.0

This update rolls up everything since 1.13.102.0.

Fixed

  • Local transcription and memory no longer break with a "corrupted model" error. On-device model storage moved out of the macOS-protected Documents folder, so a system update or app re-sign can no longer lock dooze out of its own Whisper and Gemma models. Existing models migrate automatically, and a stuck install now recovers and re-downloads instead of dead-ending on Retry.
  • You stay signed in across app updates. Updating no longer occasionally signs you out.
  • Voice dictation is faster and cleaner. Long dictation no longer slows down as you keep speaking, a seam that could drop or duplicate words at boundaries is fixed, and spurious mid-sentence periods before a conjunction are smoothed to commas.

New

  • Bring your own Claude agent into chat. Run an agentic Claude session inside dooze with your own model and thinking-effort, image and tagged-meeting context, a plan picker, a follow-up queue, and session resume across app restarts.
  • Markup & Capture. Annotate what's on screen — boxes and comments — and send the marked-up capture as context, with multiple captures stacked.

Also

  • Read Aloud now shows and plays your downloaded Premium voices.
  • Chat panel polish: the composer no longer overflows the panel edge, and the conversation stops scrolling into empty whitespace.

What's new in dooze 1.13.102.0

This update rolls up everything since 1.13.93.0.

New

  • Calendar in the meeting recorder. The New meeting panel now shows your next calendar meeting and lets you choose which calendars it watches. It reads your synced macOS calendars on-device — nothing leaves your Mac.
  • Higher-quality meeting video. Screen recordings capture at your display's native resolution in HEVC, with a Quality picker (down to audio-only) so you can trade file size for fidelity.

Improved

  • Simpler chat panel. A cleaner two-zone layout — window controls on top, and a pinned conversation line with a New chat button plus a Recent switcher below.
  • Lighter launcher. The three filled pills are now lighter icon-and-label rows, with Settings reachable from a quiet gear in the header.

Fixed

  • Voice dictation no longer duplicates speech or drops words at sentence boundaries.
  • Google sign-in reliably surfaces its window and no longer collapses the panel mid-sign-in.
  • The launcher no longer gets stuck in a clipped state.

What's new in 1.13.93.0

Fixed

  • Redeemed cloud credit no longer vanishes — cloud models stay unlocked after redeem, refresh, and relaunch. With subscription tiers removed, cloudCreditCents became the *sole* client-side gate for cloud models, which exposed three pre-existing credit-read bugs: a user who redeemed a code could get bounced back to local-only with an "out of credit" prompt because the client read 0. Three fixes: (C1) cold-start persistence — CachedAuthState now stores cloudCreditCents, so credit (and cloud access) survives quit-and-relaunch instead of reading 0 until /auth/me returns; the cache decode tolerates an older blob that predates the field. (C2) live self-heal — the chat stream now reads the server's remaining_credit_cents; when the server reports the balance is empty mid-session, the client re-locks cloud and shows the "cloud credit empty, using local" banner immediately instead of lagging a poll. (C3) stale-refresh guard — a just-redeemed balance is protected for 60s against a stale, eventually-consistent /auth/me that would otherwise clobber it back to 0; legitimate per-request decreases still flow through (the guard arms only on top-ups, applies on both the foreground and background refresh paths). (Sources/DoozeClient/Auth/AuthManager.swift, Sources/DoozeClient/API/{DoozeAPIClient,DoozeAPIModels}.swift, Sources/DoozeClient/Auth/AuthProviding.swift.)

Changed

  • Account state is now gated purely on credit, with a single "account suspended" ban — all other status gating is gone. There are no paid tiers and waitlist was retired, so the client no longer gates anything on account status: the status monotonicity guard, the optimistic-status flip on redeem, and the dead .waitlist upgrade-prompt case are all removed. The one thing status still does is a hard ban: when the server returns a 403 account_suspended, the chat panel shows a dedicated "Your account is suspended. Contact support…" message with no buy-credit or redeem call-to-action (credit can't lift a ban). A shared 403 recognizer maps the suspended response consistently across the chat, non-streaming, and TTS paths. (Sources/DoozeClient/Components/{UpgradePromptView,AskAIView}.swift, Sources/DoozeClient/API/DoozeAPIClient.swift.)
  • Tests: CreditPersistenceTests (cache round-trip + tolerant decode + the exact suspended-403 contract), AuthManagerTests (C3 stale-refresh race matrix), DoozeAPIClientTests (stream self-heal fires before the stream closes), UpgradeLimitTypeTests (suspended mapping/copy, waitlist retired). Pre-landing review (dual adversarial passes, both repos) + planning eng review (Claude + Codex) clean.

What's new in 1.13.80.0

Fixed

  • The floating meeting-recorder panel now grows when you expand it, so the Stop / Pause / Bookmark controls stay reachable during a live recording. A beta user on an older macOS still hit the 4×-regressed bug (#168 / #190 / #383): tapping the expand chevron grew the SwiftUI content to ~280pt but the NSPanel window stayed at its ~48pt compact height, so NSHostingView center-clipped the content — only the middle (streaming transcript) showed, with the control row clipped off-screen, leaving a live mic + system-audio capture with no in-panel way to stop it. Root cause (on-device-confirmed via the new release os.Logger trace, macOS 26.3.2): hosting.sizingOptions = [] froze NSHostingView.fittingSize at the compact 48pt, so every fittingSize-based resize trigger (the #383 frame observer, plus an interim layout() driver) read 48 and never asked the window to grow; the only signal that had ever reported the true expanded height was a SwiftUI GeometryReader callback, which measured the window-constrained (compressed) size — full on newer macOS, 48 on the beta user's older OS, which is why it shipped "working" four times. Fix: drop sizingOptions = [] so fittingSize computes correctly (matching the in-production FirstMouseHostingView, which runs the same config on macOS 26 without the #152/#190 updateAnimatedWindowSize crash — empirically reconfirmed no-crash on 26.3.2, the strictest crash environment); add AutoSizingRecordingHostingView, an NSHostingView subclass whose layout() drives the hosting frame to fittingSize via a deferred dispatch (crash-safe — never a synchronous setFrameSize in layout()) as the cross-OS resize trigger; the panel's frame observer now reads the clamped hosting frame instead of unclamped fittingSize; the transcript band is capped by the live screen height (maxTranscriptHeight, floor 160 / ceiling 400) so the expanded panel can't run off the bottom of a short display; a "Listening for speech…" empty state replaces the blank band; the Stop button surfaces the geometry-independent ⌘⇧R stop hint (the global hotkey stops a recording even if the panel ever mis-sizes); and a release-safe os.Logger trace (subsystem app.dooze.client, category RecordingPanel) logs the full resize chain so any recurrence on a beta machine is self-diagnosing with one log stream. Routed through /autoplan (CEO + Design + Eng dual-voice, Claude + Codex — which overturned the original "remove the callback, keep the observer" plan as a 5th-regression risk) → /review (Claude + Codex adversarial — Codex caught that removing [] re-exposed the crash path under the pulsing animation and that the observer re-read unclamped fittingSize; both fixed) → on-device verification on macOS 26.3.2 (the step all four prior fixes skipped): fittingSize 48→231 on expand, panel grows, controls visible, no crash. Verified by 20 MLX-free RecordingPanel* tests (geometry + maxTranscriptHeight cap + coalesce-gate lifecycle); swift build clean. Follow-ups filed P2/P3 in TODOS.md: re-add the graceful-degradation top-pin (keeping the hosting view as the contentView), recompute the transcript cap on didChangeScreenParametersNotification, and extract a shared CoalescedPanelResizer (now 5 hand-rolled copies). (Sources/DoozeClient/Meeting/MeetingRecordingPanel.swift, Sources/DoozeClient/Meeting/MeetingRecordingPlayerView.swift, Tests/DoozeClientTests/Meeting/RecordingPanelGeometryTests.swift.)

What's new in 1.13.78.0

Fixed

  • @-mentioning a meeting in Ask AI now works with on-device (local) models, not just cloud. Tagging a meeting with @ and asking about it (e.g. "what were the action items?") silently returned nothing useful on a local Gemma model, while the same question worked on a cloud model — so the context looked "incompatible" with local. Root cause was simpler: it was never being served to the local model at all. Both paths resolve the same meeting block, but only the cloud request forwarded it; the local prompt builder (ContextAssembler.assembleLocalMessages) had no parameter for meeting context, so the text was dropped before it ever reached MLX. Fix: thread the resolved meeting block into the local system prompt (appended last, after memory + selected-text context). Two issues a dual-voice plan review caught and fixed in the same change: (1) window overflow — the meeting block can be ~4000 tokens and the local system prompt is never trimmed (only history is), so on the smallest shipped model (phi-3.5-mini @ 4096) an unclamped block would overflow the window and leave no room to generate; a new clampMeetingBlock truncates the block to fit (keeping the high-density header/summary/notes, trimming the transcript tail). Gemma E2B @ 8192 — the reported model — never overflowed; the clamp protects the smaller models the fix would otherwise have regressed. (2) privacy parity — the resolver was hardwired to the cloud-safe (attendee-name-redacted) transcript; local now uses the richer speaker-attributed fullTranscriptText via a new TranscriptDestination (.cloud default preserves the redaction contract + privacy sentinel tests; only local turns opt into .local), justified because local injection is on-device with no network egress and the transcript is already at rest. The model selection is captured once at submit so the destination decision and the inference path can't disagree (a cloud turn can never ship the un-redacted transcript). Routed through /investigate → /autoplan (CEO + Eng; Codex unavailable this run due to a gpt-5.5 CLI fault, so Claude single-voice with independent subagents — which overturned the original "overflow is acceptable" call and added the clamp) → /review (adversarial pass; surfaced 3 narrow follow-ups, all filed to TODOS.md: multi-meeting drop + explicit-vs-memory priority on the 4096 model, and a pre-existing attendee-name header that egresses to cloud). Manually validated in-app: a local model now answers from @-tagged meeting content, and the cloud path is unchanged. Verified by 30 MLX-free tests (PromptAssemblyTests incl. present/absent/overflow-budget/three-block-ordering, MeetingContextResolverTests destination selection) plus the CloudPrivacy* and PreSendSecretGate sentinels staying green; build clean. (Sources/DoozeClient/Context/ContextAssembler.swift, Sources/DoozeClient/Meeting/MeetingContextResolver.swift, Sources/DoozeClient/Components/AppContainer.swift.)

What's new in 1.13.68.0

Added

  • On-device memory extraction now actually runs for everyone — the Brain's Gemma E2B model auto-downloads in the background instead of silently never being fetched. The Brain hardcodes E2B for every memory/extraction skill and no-ops silently if the model isn't on disk, but E2B was only downloaded when it happened to be the RAM-selected *chat* tier — i.e. only on <16 GB Macs. On 16 GB+ Macs (the majority) the onboarding picker chose E4B/12B for chat, E2B was never fetched, and on-device memory extraction silently never ran. E2B now downloads from the same post-sign-in point that already auto-downloads Whisper (covering OAuth sign-in + onboarding completion), and re-triggers at the head of every Brain ingest as a demand-driven fallback for users whose download failed or never ran — idempotent, non-blocking, and additive to (not a replacement for) the user's chosen chat model. The download policy lives in LocalModelService.triggerMemoryModelDownloadIfNeeded (not in AuthManager): a pure MemoryModelDownloadGate truth table decides *whether* to fetch (only .notDownloaded/.downloadError), a NetworkMonitor.isExpensive/isConstrained gate defers the ~3.58 GB fetch off metered/hotspot links, and a 60 s failure backoff stops a relaunch/auth loop from re-thrashing. Download serialization (correctness): LocalModelService.downloadModel actually cold-loads the model into MLX/GPU (not just bytes), so it now runs at most one download at a time process-wide via a FIFO lane — E2B and the chat-tier model can no longer stack two concurrent GPU constructions during onboarding on a 16 GB Mac; queued models keep their real state (never overloaded as .downloading). Stall watchdog: a download that makes no byte progress for 120 s is cancelled and marked .downloadError so a hung transfer can't wedge the serial lane and block the chat model, with the gate retrying later. Privacy-safe Sentry breadcrumbs (memory_model.download.{triggered,skipped,deferred}, model.download.{queued,stalled}) make the funnel observable. Reviewed via /autoplan dual-voice (CEO + Eng, Claude + Codex) on the plan and /review on the diff (which added the queue-state-overload fix, the stall watchdog, the network-cost injection seam, and the backoff/skip coverage). 21 MLX-free unit tests across MemoryModelDownloadGateTests, TriggerMemoryModelDownloadTests, LocalModelServiceDownloadQueueTests, and LocalModelServiceDownloadWatchdogTests. Follow-ups (a true download-only backend path that doesn't cold-load GPU, a preload/idle-band mutex audit, tier-aware cloud-vs-local memory routing, and a user-visible memory-state surface) are filed P3 in TODOS.md. (Sources/DoozeClient/Services/{LocalModelService,NetworkMonitor,MemoryModelDownloadGate}.swift, Sources/DoozeClient/Auth/AuthManager.swift, Sources/DoozeClient/Brain/Brain.swift.)

What's new in 1.13.47

A lot has landed since 1.9.7. The highlights:

Memory

  • Dooze now builds a private, on-device memory from your meetings, chats, and voice notes. Ask what you agreed on, who's working on what, or what your action items are, and it answers from your own history. Everything stays local and encrypted; deleting a source removes it from memory.

Meetings

  • Stop is instant. The recorder saves and opens the meeting in a second or two instead of freezing while the transcript finishes.
  • Your live transcript is never lost, even if the final pass is interrupted — recover with Retry.
  • Search across every meeting with ⌘F, or from Spotlight.
  • Cleaner transcripts: better speaker separation, fewer phantom words, and correct punctuation at pauses.
  • Play back a recording with the transcript following along; click any line to jump.

Voice dictation

  • Double-tap your dictate key to go hands-free. It keeps listening until you pause, tap again, or press Escape.
  • Long dictations no longer duplicate or interleave text.

Read aloud

  • Have Dooze read any article or selection out loud, with a redesigned voice picker and premium cloud voices.

Models & account

  • New on-device models, including a larger 12B option for capable Macs, with a clearer model picker.
  • Cloud credit. Redeem a code or top up ($5–$100) to use cloud models. Dooze falls back to local automatically when credit runs out.

Sign-in & stability

  • Reskinned sign-in and a fix for getting stuck signed out with no way back in.
  • Faster launch, lower memory use, and many crash fixes.

For the full per-version changelog, see the CHANGELOG on GitHub.

What's New in 1.9.7.1

Catch-up release rolling up everything since 1.7.1 plus a critical macOS 26 fix.

Crash fixes

  • Past meetings no longer crash the app on macOS 26.4.1. The floating panel resized its hosting view mid-display-cycle, which the new OS treats as fatal. Resizes are now deferred to the next runloop tick. Affects Polish, Chat, and Notetaker transitions too.
  • Voice dictation no longer crashes during the waveform animation. Capture-thread/UI-thread race on WhisperKit's audio energy buffer narrowed to a single property read.

New

  • Ask AI about your meetings. Type @ in chat to mention a meeting by name. The AI gets the meeting's summary, notes, and a transcript excerpt so it can answer questions about what was discussed and what was decided.
  • Meeting knowledge extraction. Key facts, commitments, and people from each meeting are automatically extracted into your memory vault. Meetings shorter than a minute are skipped.

Sign-in & sessions

  • Switching back to the app no longer logs you out. Profile refresh on resume retries with a fresh token. Network errors keep you offline instead of signing you out.
  • Sign-in can be cancelled. A cancel button appears during OAuth sign-in, with a 15-second timeout so you're never stuck waiting on a hung server.
  • Logout is local-only on error paths. Only explicit sign-out from Settings revokes the server-side session, preventing accidental session destruction.

Voice & Read Aloud

  • Music pauses and resumes correctly with Spotify. Now uses the dedicated playback-state symbol that all NowPlaying apps populate, not just the rate field Spotify ignores.
  • Music actually stays paused for the full dictation session. The async capture/sync pause race that recorded "wasPlaying = false" and never resumed is fixed.
  • Read aloud in chat stays inline. Tapping "Read aloud" plays in a compact pill next to the message instead of opening a separate panel.

Meetings & Notetaker

  • Past meetings sorted newest-first. Date groups now run reverse chronologically below Today and Yesterday.
  • Text selection works in transcripts and notes. Select and copy across speakers; bookmark jumps still scroll to the right segment.
  • Meeting context pills no longer overlap the chat input. The pill now sits above the text field as a sibling to slash-command pills.

For the full per-version changelog, see the CHANGELOG on GitHub.

What's New in 1.7.1

Critical bug-fix release for issues found in 1.7.0.

  • Fixed crash on mini-player expand/collapse during active recording
  • Fixed silent meeting playback — recordings now play with full audio
  • Fixed duplicate words at transcription segment boundaries
  • Fixed voice dictation finalize — releasing fn now reliably ends the session
  • Fixed second voice dictation being silently rejected after the first finished
  • Music now pauses during dictation and resumes when you're done
  • Long meeting pauses no longer lose their silence audio
  • Memory retrieval now prefers high-confidence facts under tight token budgets

What's New in 1.7.0

  • Read Aloud. Listen to anything — paste, a URL, or live clipboard. Use your Mac's premium voices for free, or switch to high-quality cloud voices
  • Voice Mini-Player. Compact player with history, scrub, and instant interrupt-replace. Voice and mode controls live inside the player
